title: AirPrompter root metadata (key-set)
description: TUF-shaped root of trust (D53). `signed` lists the online `targets` keys that may sign manifests, with a threshold and an expiry, and is itself signed by the offline `root` keys. The root public key is pinned in SDK source; rotating a signing key is a new root document signed by root, so a compromised signing key can never authorize its successor. Customer countersign key-sets use the same shape with `purpose: countersign`.

purpose.description: `platform`: AirPrompter's manifest signing keys. `countersign`: a customer's release keys (§6.3).

environment.description: The hosted environment this root governs (one platform key per environment, D43). Customer key-sets name the target they countersign for.

version.description: Strictly increasing per (purpose, environment). A runtime refuses a root document older than the one it holds.

expires.description: After this instant a runtime treats the root as expired: it refuses NEW manifests, keeps serving the active release, and reports `root_expired`. 90 days from the ceremony is the platform default.

signatures.description: Root-role signatures over the canonical JSON of `signed`. At least `roles.root.threshold` must verify against keys listed in `roles.root.keyIds` of the root document the runtime already trusts (the pinned root, or the previous version in a chain).

publicKey.description: The public key as a JWK. `keyId` is expected to be its RFC 7638 thumbprint.

notAfter.description: Optional per-key expiry, used during an overlap rotation so the old key ages out without a further ceremony.
